original_question: Do there exist 2-type surfaces that lie fully in an even-dimensional hypersphere of a Euclidean space? In particular, do there exist mass-symmetric 2-type surfaces that lie fully in an even-dimensional hypersphere?
target_in_paper: Section 3.3, Problem 7, in the subsection "2-type Spherical Surfaces of Higher Codimension"; this is the exact open problem your draft is aiming at. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper: it preserves both the main existence question about 2-type surfaces in even-dimensional hyperspheres and the sharper sub-question about the mass-symmetric case. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))
missing_details: The paper uses Chen's spectral notion of 2-type: for the position vector x of the immersion, one has a spectral decomposition x = c + x_1 + x_2 with Δx_i = λ_i x_i for the Laplacian Δ of the induced metric, and the two eigenvalues are distinct. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))

A "surface" here means a connected 2-dimensional manifold immersed in a real Euclidean space E^N and equipped with the metric induced from that ambient Euclidean space. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))

To make the question stand-alone, the ambient sphere should be written explicitly as some even-dimensional hypersphere S^{2m} ⊂ E^{2m+1}; the surrounding subsection is specifically about higher codimension, so the intended nontrivial cases are the ones with m ≥ 2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))

The phrase "mass-symmetric" must be defined: if the surface lies in a hypersphere, then the constant vector c in the spectral decomposition is required to be the center of that hypersphere. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))

The phrase "lie fully" is left implicit in Section 3.3; to make the problem self-contained, it should be stated as a full immersion into S^{2m}, in the standard sense that the image is not contained in a proper subsphere of S^{2m}. This is a clarifying reformulation of the paper's wording, not a new hypothesis. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))

The paper asks only for existence; it should not be broadened into a classification problem, nor into questions about arbitrary k-type surfaces or all codimensions. Section 3.3 says this problem is more general than Problem 5, but still specifically about even-dimensional hyperspheres. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))
refined_question: Does there exist a connected surface M^2 and a full isometric immersion x: M^2 → S^{2m} ⊂ E^{2m+1} for some m ≥ 2, where "full" means x(M) is not contained in a proper subsphere of S^{2m}, such that x is of Chen 2-type with respect to the Laplacian Δ of the induced metric, i.e. x = c + x_1 + x_2 and Δx_i = λ_i x_i with λ_1 ≠ λ_2? More specifically, can such a surface be mass-symmetric, meaning that the constant vector c equals the center of S^{2m}? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))
justification: Section 3.3 states this as Problem 7 and explicitly presents it as a generalization of Problem 5. The only nearby definitions needed to make the question mathematically self-contained are the Section 1 definitions of k-type and mass-symmetry. Accordingly, the rewrite keeps the problem at exactly the paper's level of scope—an existence question—and only makes explicit the ambient real Euclidean sphere, the spectral meaning of 2-type, and the implicit meanings of "full" and "mass-symmetric." ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1307.6582))
